results.name: Tripoli
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the people of Tripoli had to shut down their own city to be heard. Residents blocked roads and closed public buildings across at least six districts from 26 to 28 July 2026 over daily power cuts, water outages and a failing health system, and Al Jazeera reported that the electricity crisis sits inside a control fight between the Prime Minister and the state power company’s chairman.

results.name: PepsiCo
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a worker says she told PepsiCo about anti-gay harassment for two years and it kept happening. She sued on 24 July 2026 in federal court in Pennsylvania, alleging coworkers refused to share a restroom with her and used a homophobic slur; PepsiCo has not responded and no court has ruled, so the claim moves the Empathy score by only 0.1 raw points.

results.name: Comcast
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the allegation is that humiliation was scheduled. A former Comcast retail worker in Plainville, Connecticut says the store manager had the top salesperson tie the lowest-ranked salesperson to a chair each month and smash a cream pie in their face; Comcast says it disagrees with the claims and no court has ruled, so no score was moved on the allegation.

results.name: Tacoma
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the thing Tacoma was flagged for is not Tacoma’s doing. The paused health inspections concern the Northwest ICE Processing Center, which GEO Group owns and operates under a federal contract; the State of Washington sued and a federal appeals court paused the order, and the City of Tacoma is not a party to any of it.

results.name: Whole Foods Market
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a case ending is not the same as a case being answered. A federal court dismissed a former Whole Foods worker’s discrimination claim on 24 July 2026 on a filing deadline, not on the merits, so nothing in the record establishes that the alleged conduct did not occur — and the score was not moved upward on it.

results.name: Xcel Energy
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Xcel Energy was flagged for a fire it has not been shown to have started. The Aspen Acres lawsuit filed on 16 July 2026 names San Isabel Electric Association, not Xcel, and Colorado’s fire authority says the cause is still under investigation, so the claim was dropped as a wrong-entity attribution and no score was moved.

results.name: Costa Rica
results.key_finding: Why it matters: nothing has been passed yet. Costa Rica’s president delivered six security bills on 27 July 2026, but the headline constitutional amendment widening extradition of Costa Rican citizens was not filed and is due on 3 August 2026, so it was not scored — and the score was confirmed at 81.4 with a watch flag.

results.name: Goldman Sachs
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a court has now found that Goldman Sachs punished a man for using the bank’s own parental leave policy. A London employment tribunal awarded Jonathan Reeves £1.45 million, about $1.93 million, for sex discrimination and unfair dismissal after six months of parental leave, and Goldman said it strongly disagrees with the decision.

results.name: Northrop Grumman
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the plant is designed to emit one-tenth of a ton less than the amount that would trigger stricter federal rules. Northrop Grumman’s proposed Waynesboro permit caps combined hazardous air pollutants at 24.9 tons a year against a 25-ton federal major-source threshold, and more than 50 residents told Virginia regulators on 23 July 2026 that they do not believe the limit protects them.

results.name: American Airlines
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the outage itself is not the finding — the repetition is. American Airlines halted every departure nationwide for about 48 minutes on 28 July 2026 and nobody was hurt, but reporting identifies it as the third FAA ground stop in under two years from the same connectivity failure in the airline’s own systems.

results.name: Nepal
results.key_finding: Why it matters: a doctor was beaten and the country stopped treating people. After Dr Pramod Ram was assaulted at Narayani Hospital in Birgunj on 25 July 2026, the Nepal Medical Association halted all non-emergency care nationwide for two days, and Nepal is scored not for the shutdown — which the association called — but for failing to protect health workers from a pattern of assault.

results.name: Portugal
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Portugal has made it a fineable offence to cover your face in public. Parliament passed the ban on 17 July 2026 with a two-thirds majority and fines of €200 to €4,000, and Amnesty International Portugal’s executive director said the law "is discriminatory and is a threat to human rights" because it still falls on Muslim women who cover their faces.

results.name: CVS Health
results.key_finding: Why it matters: the money was supposed to pay for care for people who cannot afford it. Two Michigan hospital systems allege CVS Health improperly kept about $95 million in 340B drug pricing savings meant for low-income patients, and that CVS refused a contractually required audit and then cancelled Henry Ford’s 340B contracts — allegations CVS has not yet answered.

results.name: Fudan University
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Fudan was flagged for something the Pentagon did, not something Fudan did. The U.S. Department of War added Fudan to its research-security list on 23 July 2026 alongside 130 institutions in China, Russia and Iran, which says nothing about how Fudan treats students, staff or the public — so the claim was screened out and no score moved.

results.name: Hawaii
results.key_finding: Why it matters: Hawaii charged its own second-highest official. A grand jury indicted Lieutenant Governor Sylvia Luke on 25 July 2026 on 12 counts including bribery over an alleged 2022 scheme, brought by the state’s own Attorney General — an individual’s alleged conduct and a functioning accountability system, not an institutional compassion failure, so the score holds at 56.3 with a difference of exactly zero.

results.name: Singapore
results.key_finding: Why it matters: nothing happened in this window, and that is the finding. A dedicated search across lawsuits, labour, safety, regulatory and humanitarian signals found no compassion-relevant Singapore evidence between 16 and 30 July 2026, so the score is confirmed at 62.2 on standing structural context alone.

A dedicated search found no compassion-relevant Mauritius evidence between 16 and 30 July 2026, and the -1.9 arithmetic difference is a pre-existing index reconstruction discrepancy of 1.6 plus grid rounding, not a conduct finding.

results.key_finding: Why it matters: nothing happened in this window, and that is the finding. A dedicated search found no compassion-relevant Andorra evidence between 16 and 30 July 2026, and the -1.9 difference is entirely a rounding artifact of the scoring grid, not a conduct finding.

results.key_finding: Why it matters: nothing happened in this window, and that is the finding. A dedicated search found no compassion-relevant Erie Indemnity evidence between 16 and 30 July 2026, so the score is confirmed at 60.9 on standing context alone, including an unresolved January 2026 claim that a customer paid higher premiums for years because of another person’s data in her file.

results.name: Dollar General
results.key_finding: Why it matters: nothing happened in this window, and that is the finding. A dedicated search found no compassion-relevant Dollar General evidence between 16 and 30 July 2026, so the score is confirmed at 21.9 with a difference of exactly zero, resting on the July 2024 $12 million federal safety settlement that followed more than a decade of wilful violations.

claims_dropped_on_verification.claim: Investigators identified an "unmoored" Xcel Energy power line spark as one of two ignition points of the Aspen Acres fire; lawsuit filed around 16 July 2026.
claims_dropped_on_verification.reason: WRONG ENTITY. The Colorado Sun (2026-07-16) was fetched directly and names San Isabel Electric Association as the defendant; the plaintiffs are four property owners alleging a downed power line and uncleared vegetation. Xcel Energy appears in that article only in a reference to the separate 2021 Marshall fire settlement. Colorado Public Radio (2026-07-16) names the same defendant. The Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control states the cause remains under investigation. No in-window dated source attributes an Aspen Acres ignition point to an Xcel asset. Claim dropped; no score moved on it.

claims_dropped_on_verification.claim: U.S. Department of War (Pentagon) added Fudan University to its Section 1286 research-security list on 23 July 2026.
claims_dropped_on_verification.reason: ATTRIBUTION. The event is verified and correctly dated, but it is the conduct of the United States government, not of Fudan University. It describes nothing Fudan did to anyone it serves. Under the attribution rule it cannot move Fudan score in either direction, and treating a foreign national-security designation as a compassion finding would import an unrelated judgment into the benchmark. No score moved on it.

claims_dropped_on_verification.claim: Ninth Circuit administrative stay (21-24 July 2026) pausing health and safety inspections at the GEO Group-run Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma.
claims_dropped_on_verification.reason: ATTRIBUTION. Verified and correctly dated, but the actors are GEO Group (refused entry), the State of Washington (won the injunction), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (contracting agency) and a federal appellate panel (granted the stay). The City of Tacoma is not a party and does not own or operate the facility. No score moved on it. Tacoma own detention-adjacent conduct, Ordinance No. 29105 and Resolution No. 41757, falls in May 2026, outside the window, and is recorded as standing context only.

claims_dropped_on_verification.claim: Lieutenant Governor Sylvia Luke and four others indicted on 25 July 2026 on bribery and conspiracy charges.
claims_dropped_on_verification.reason: ATTRIBUTION, both directions. The alleged conduct is an individual and dates to 2022, when Luke chaired the state House Finance Committee, so it is not the state institutional conduct and does not support a downgrade. The within-window institutional act is the Hawaii Attorney General office charging a sitting Lieutenant Governor and the Governor calling for her resignation, which is accountability machinery working. An upgrade eleven days after the fresh 2026-07-19 evidence-based baseline would be assessor-to-assessor variance, so it was declined. Confirmed at delta exactly 0.

claims_dropped_on_verification.claim: Nationwide FAA ground stop on 28 July 2026 following an IT/connectivity outage.
claims_dropped_on_verification.reason: THRESHOLD. Verified and correctly dated, but a 48-minute operational outage with no injuries is not automatically institutional harm and was not scored as harm. Only two elements were scored: the third recurrence of the same connectivity failure mode in under two years (Christmas Eve 2024, June 2025, 28 July 2026), which is a Systemic Learning finding, and the simultaneous unavailability of the app and website, which is a passenger-channel finding.

claims_dropped_on_verification.claim: Federal court in Washington, D.C. dismissed a former worker discrimination suit on 24 July 2026.
claims_dropped_on_verification.reason: DIRECTIONALITY. A dismissal is not automatically favourable conduct. The court dismissed on a filing-deadline point, not on the merits, so nothing in the record establishes that the alleged conduct did not occur. Scoring it as exculpatory would have produced a false-positive upgrade. It was not scored positively.

claims_dropped_on_verification.claim: Constitutional amendment widening extradition of Costa Rican nationals, delivered 27 July 2026.
claims_dropped_on_verification.reason: PROSPECTIVE ACT. The Tico Times (2026-07-27) states the constitutional text was NOT among the files handed to the Legislative Assembly, because legislative procedure does not allow constitutional reforms in extraordinary sessions, and that the government would file it on 3 August 2026, after the close of this evidence window. An unfiled bill was not scored. The six security bills that were delivered are recorded and watch-flagged.

notes.scoring_mechanics: No assessment in this cycle had its delta driven by the integration premium. Every entity except Costa Rica had the weakness factor at 0 in both the published and assessed sets, so no premium applied to either and all movement was base composite. Costa Rica had exactly one sub-4.0 dimension in both sets, so its 8.0-point premium was identical in both and contributed nothing to the difference; a second sub-4.0 dimension would have stripped 2.0 further points, and that amplification was deliberately avoided by not scoring an unfiled bill. This cycle is therefore the Carnegie Mellon (2026-07-29) case throughout, not the Taipei (2026-07-28) case.

band_crossings_considered.reason: A harsher but arguable reading of the 17 July 2026 face-covering ban would have moved Portugal from Established to Functional. It was not adopted. Band crossings require at least two sources with at least one at tier 4 or above; the law human rights characterisation rests on a single tier-3 source (Amnesty International) with no treaty body, Council of Europe or court assessment yet. The proposal was filed at -5.0 with band unchanged and recommendation flag-for-review.
